Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API eval - quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about how Acme AI plans to add an assistant and embeddings to your product. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed: 

- Goal: Evaluate Hosted API for an initial integration (chat + semantic search).
- Evaluation length: 2–3 weeks pilot — ramping on dev -> staging -> prod traffic.
- Key asks from your side: rate limits/concurrency, data residency (EU), and whether we can spike capacity during demo days.

Quickstart & endpoints:
1) API key: you should have received the test key via the portal (let me know if not).
2) Endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat for chat + POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings for embeddings.
3) Sample curl (chat):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \\
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \\
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
     -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize our Q1 roadmap."}]}'

Rate limits (Hosted API):
- Default soft limits: 60 requests/minute and 10 concurrent requests per org.
- Token throughput: turn-based token rate limits vary by model; typical sustained throughput ~60k tokens/min for the medium family.
- Spikes: we can temporarily raise soft limits for demos or launches (requires a quick support request and 24–48h lead time for guaranteed bursts).

If you expect steady high throughput (multiple hundreds of concurrent requests / sustained throughput guarantees) we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity). For strict compliance and on-prem needs, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is available. For this evaluation, Hosted API should be the fastest path.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm target p95 latency (ms) and expected average and peak requests/sec for the pilot?
- I’ve attached the quick SOC/infosec checklist we discussed (cc Marissa for any technical follow-ups).
- If it helps, Marissa can schedule a 30m tech onboarding to walk your engineers through the quickstart and test endpoints.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Samantha —

Answers inline:

- Spikes: Yes — Hosted API supports temporary burst increases. For your planned demo days we can submit a support change to raise the soft concurrency and RPS limits for the demo window. Lead time: best-effort within 24 hours, SLA-backed increases require Dedicated. I’ll add details in HubSpot and open the support ticket once you confirm exact demo windows.

- EU data residency: We have EU-hosted regions and the Hosted API will process eval traffic within the EU region when you select the EU endpoint. No replication to other regions for customer data by default; we can provide the region-processing SLA language for procurement.

- Security questionnaire: Thanks for sending — I’ve forwarded to our security team and they’ll return a filled checklist and any clarifying notes by EOD next business day.

If you’d like predictable throughput for production with capacity commitments and no manual support tickets to raise limits, Redwood Dedicated is the recommended path — we can build a mutual action plan and a simple capacity commitment. For strict regulatory/air-gapped requirements, Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) is the route. For evaluation, Hosted API + an agreed burst window should be the fastest.

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm demo windows and expected peak timestamps so I can open a support ticket for the burst.
2) Marissa to schedule a 30m technical onboarding with your engineers (she’ll cover quickstart, SDK, and sample load tests).
3) We’ll have security return the questionnaire and provide EU-region SLA language.

Marissa — can you propose Tue/Wed next week slots?

Thanks,
Neha
